original_question: Does every complete intersection have the Weak Lefschetz Property, meaning that multiplication by a general linear form has maximal rank in the case d = 1?
target_in_paper: Section 2 ("Monomial level algebras"), in the discussion immediately after Theorem 2.12 and before Theorem 2.13. The nearest paper-faithful target is the informal open problem stated there: although monomial complete intersections have the WLP by Theorem 2.3, "it is not known (except in codimension ≤ 3, as noted below) whether all complete intersections have this property." ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the topic (complete intersections), the property in question (the Weak Lefschetz Property), and the operative d = 1 formulation: multiplication by a general linear form should have maximal rank. That matches the paper’s definition of WLP given right after Theorem 2.3. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s nearby discussion is about Artinian homogeneous complete intersections in a standard graded polynomial ring, not arbitrary complete intersections in every possible sense. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
You need the ambient data: R = K[x_1, ..., x_r], I subset R homogeneous, and A = R/I. The maps are between graded pieces A_i and A_{i+1}. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

To make "complete intersection" stand-alone here, one should say that I is generated by a homogeneous regular sequence; in the Artinian case this gives a finite-dimensional graded algebra A. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The characteristic-zero hypothesis is missing. The nearby WLP statements in this section are explicitly over a field of characteristic zero, and the paper warns that the monomial complete-intersection theorem can fail in positive characteristic. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The quantifier "for every degree" is missing: WLP means that for a general linear form L, the map times L: A_i -> A_{i+1} has maximal rank for every i, not just in one unspecified degree. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The open problem in this paper is sharper than your wording because codimension ≤ 3 is already noted as known; the genuinely open range is higher codimension. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

Your draft does not distinguish the nearby proved theorem from the open question: Theorem 2.3 is only for Artinian monomial complete intersections and in fact proves the stronger property that times L^d has maximal rank for all positive d and all i; the paper then asks whether the d = 1 property extends to all complete intersections. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
refined_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let R = K[x_1, ..., x_r], and let I = (f_1, ..., f_r) be an Artinian homogeneous complete intersection in R (equivalently, f_1, ..., f_r is a homogeneous regular sequence, so A = R/I is finite-dimensional). For r >= 4, must A have the Weak Lefschetz Property; that is, for a general linear form L in R_1, is the multiplication map times L: A_i -> A_{i+1} of maximal rank for every integer i?
justification: The draft is not aiming at a numbered conjecture in this paper; the nearest exact target is the informal open problem in Section 2. Theorem 2.3 first proves, for Artinian monomial complete intersections over characteristic 0, the stronger maximal-rank statement for times L^d in every degree, and the text immediately after it defines WLP as the d = 1 case. Later, after Theorem 2.12, the authors explicitly note that monomial complete intersections in any codimension have the WLP, but that it is still unknown whether all complete intersections do, except that codimension 3 is known via the syzygy-bundle approach discussed just before Theorem 2.13. Hence the sharp stand-alone reformulation should be stated for Artinian homogeneous complete intersections over characteristic 0 and should isolate the open codimension range r >= 4. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
